messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate detected on /v1/generate in us-west-2. error_rate=12% over 5m, spikes correlated with streaming requests. auto-escalation to #eng-oncall.

alice (oncall): I'm on it. @bob can you grab customer-impact? which orgs are hitting errors?

bob (oncall): early look: 4 tenants showing >20% failed requests, highest QPS from a video-transcription customer. Errors are 502/503 gateway responses. No DB alerts.

sam (infra): rolling logs: upstream runtime OOMs around KV cache pressure, looks like blob of long-context streaming sessions. Suggest immediate traffic shaping at the edge: reduce per-connection concurrency + apply soft rate limit to non-enterprise orgs.

lee (eng-runtime): we can also spin down the long-context worker pool or fallback streaming requests to a smaller model variant until stabilized. Fallback preserves latency but reduces memory.

marie (devex): we should push out quick SDK guidance for customers while we mitigate. Draft guidance: increase client retry backoff to jittered exponential, cap max_retries=6, use idempotency tokens for non-streaming mutating calls, and disable automatic streaming reconnects for transient 5xx. I'll paste a short snippet for us to send to customers and include in release notes.

alice (oncall): sam/lee, can you list the concrete edge changes you can make now? I'll coordinate with ops and start paging out a customer note.

sam (infra): applying soft rate limit: non-enterprise orgs set to 75% of current quota, per-org burst window 30s -> 10s. Command hitting ops API now:

ops-deploy-bot: POST https://ops-api.internal/edge/rate-limits apply {"scope":"non-enterprise","limit_pct":75,"burst_window":10}

ops-deploy-bot: throttles applied (request id 9f3a2). Monitoring: p50 latency unchanged, 5xx trend starting to drop.

lee (eng-runtime): disabled fast_stream feature flag for all non-enterprise traffic:

ops-deploy-bot: PATCH https://ops-api.internal/flags/fast_stream {"state":"off","target":"non-enterprise"}

lee (eng-runtime): also queued a model-variant fallback for streaming endpoints so new streaming sessions land on a quantized small-medium model. Should reduce memory pressure.

marie (devex): customer SDK guidance (copyable):

```
# Recommended temporary client changes (applies to hosted API consumers)
# 1) Backoff: switch to jittered exponential backoff
max_retries = 6
base_delay = 0.2  # seconds
max_delay = 5.0
# pseudo-code
for attempt in range(max_retries):
    wait = min(max_delay, base_delay * (2 ** attempt))
    jitter = random.uniform(0, wait * 0.3)
    sleep(wait + jitter)
    resp = send_request()
    if resp.ok():
        break

# 2) Idempotency header for non-streaming mutating calls
# include a unique id per logical operation to avoid duplicate side-effects
X-Idempotency-Key: <uuid-v4>

# 3) Streaming: disable automatic retries for open streaming sessions
# retry only when connection refused / immediate connection failures; do not automatic reattach mid-stream
```

marie (devex): inline curl sample for idempotent POST:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ops -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -d '{"input":"..."}'
```

bob (oncall): drafting customer notification now: short note explaining we're applying temporary rate limits and disabling fast_stream for non-enterprise to protect stability. Link to SDK guidance and expected timeline (30-90min).

alice (oncall): handoff note: @carla you'll take over active monitoring at 18:30 UTC. I will remain available for 15m overlap. Key metrics to watch: total_5xx_rate, stream_open_count, kv_cache_evictions.

carla (oncall): acknowledged. Will monitor dashboards and escalate if 5xx > 5% or any enterprise customers report issues.

lee (eng-runtime): quick exec summary of mitigations applied: 1) soft 75% rate limit on non-enterprise orgs; 2) disabled fast_stream feature flag for non-enterprise; 3) model fallback for new streaming sessions to smaller model; 4) queued additional workers to handle backlog. Observed 5xx drop from 12% -> 3% over 8m after changes.

sam (infra): note on rollout: these are soft, reversible changes. Ops can rollback limit or re-enable fast_stream per region if we see unexpected impact. Runbook steps documented in #eng-oncall pinned thread.

marie (devex): I pushed the SDK note to the support playbook and started a short support blast for customers hitting errors. Also prepared a small snippet for the SDK packages to flip retry defaults temporarily. Will open PR after this thread.

alice (oncall): assigning post-incident follow-ups: root cause analysis (lee), capacity plan for KV cache (sam), customer comms recap (marie). Due EOD tomorrow.

ops-deploy-bot: metrics: error_rate_us-west-2 = 2.8% (5m), stream_open_count = -60% from peak, kv_cache_evictions trending down.

carla (oncall): taking 18:30 handoff. Leaving pinned checklist: keep rate limits in place until 2h steady state, then gradually relax in 15% increments while watching 5xx.

alice (oncall): thanks team. If any enterprise customers show regression we will prioritize rollback per org. Closing active page, moving to monitoring-only. Will start postmortem doc once logs fully retained. :thumbsup:
